title: The 6-Ton Amber Room Stolen in 36 Hours 👑
hook_sentence: In 1941, German soldiers of Army Group North disassembled the Amber Room in 36 hours under expert supervision.
narration_script: In 1941, German soldiers of Army Group North disassembled the Amber Room in 36 hours under expert supervision. By one estimate, following eighteenth-century expansions, the completed room covered more than 590 square feet (55 sq m) and contained over 13,000 pounds (6 tonnes) of amber. In early 1944, it was packed into crates in Königsberg Castle. Documentation tracking its location ends in August 1944, when Allied bombers heavily fire-bombed Königsberg. Investigations conclude the room was most likely incinerated when Königsberg Castle was bombed by British aircraft and shelled by Soviet artillery. Yet in 1997, an original stone mosaic was recovered in Germany, fueling hunts for the chamber looted in 1941.
closing_sentence: Yet in 1997, an original stone mosaic was recovered in Germany, fueling hunts for the chamber looted in 1941.
caption:
A gilded palace chamber vanished into thin air during wartime chaos.
✨ Attempts were made to conceal the fragile amber walls from invading German forces behind mundane wallpaper inside the Catherine Palace at Tsarskoye Selo near Saint Petersburg, Russia. By one estimate, following eighteenth-century expansions, the completed room covered more than 55 square metres and contained over 6 tonnes of amber. In early 1944, as Allied forces advanced, the room was disassembled and packed into crates for storage in the Königsberg Castle basement before all documentation ended. Do you believe the lost crates survived in a secret bunker, or were they lost to the firestorms of war? 🤔
